repos.description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
repos.analysis: REA is an open-source MCP server that equips AI coding agents with reverse-engineering superpowers — analyzing closed-source app behavior, inspecting native binaries, and mapping undocumented APIs without ever needing the original source code. Developers can study any proprietary feature and reconstruct it in their own project, all without leaving their agent environment. It exploded in stars today because it bridges a real workflow gap for competitive engineers and developers building integrations against undocumented platforms. Works out of the box with any MCP-capable agent such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex.
repos.llm_api_note: MCP server — requires an MCP-compatible agent (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)

repos.description: Tool for automatic PS5 executables porting to Linux and Windows
repos.analysis: AnyPS5 is a C++ compatibility tool that automatically ports PS5 game executables to run natively on Linux and Windows — analogous to what DXVK does for DirectX titles, but targeting the PS5 hardware/OS ABI. It addresses the complete absence of any official PS5 game compatibility layer on PC, making PlayStation exclusives accessible without Sony's infrastructure. It surged today on excitement from PC gaming communities who have long requested a Wine-like solution for PS5. The target audience spans PC gaming enthusiasts, homebrew developers, and OS-compatibility researchers interested in the PS5's hardware stack.

repos.description: ArtCraft is an intentional crafting engine for artists, designers, and filmmakers
repos.analysis: ArtCraft is a desktop IDE for visual creators that lets you compose shots in 2D, stage scenes in 3D with posed characters and camera control, then send those precisely composed frames to a catalog of 62 AI generative models from providers like Grok, Midjourney, and Sora. It solves the prompt-lottery problem: rather than re-rolling prompts to get a precise image, artists build the scene first and use AI to render it, making outputs repeatable and art-directed. It is trending today on the promise of bringing production-grade creative control to consumer AI generation. Filmmakers, concept artists, and game designers who need deterministic, director-quality outputs will find it immediately useful.
repos.llm_api_note: Requires subscriptions or API keys to third-party AI providers (Midjourney, Grok, Sora, etc.)

repos.description: Editorial diagram design for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Factory Droid, and Pi. 44 diagram types.
repos.analysis: Diagram Design is an agent skill that instructs AI coding tools to produce 44 types of editorial-style diagrams as fully self-contained HTML/SVG files — no build step, no external dependencies, just one file you drop anywhere. It eliminates the copy-paste-export cycle of traditional diagramming tools: instead of wrestling with Figma or Mermaid, you describe the diagram in plain language and the agent writes it. It surged today likely because Claude Code's skill registry surfaced it to a wide audience of developer-writers. Frontend developers, technical writers, and developer-relations teams working with any MCP-compatible AI coding assistant will get immediate value.
repos.llm_api_note: Agent skill — requires Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or similar AI coding agent

repos.description: A spy satellite simulator in your browser, except the data is real.
repos.analysis: Gods Eye View is a browser-based satellite tracker that renders real-time orbital positions of active satellites and space objects using live TLE (Two-Line Element) datasets from sources like CelesTrak, wrapped in a cinematic spy-satellite aesthetic. It bridges the gap between raw orbital mechanics data and a human-comprehensible, visually compelling experience — no installation required. It is trending on the appeal of combining genuine scientific satellite data with a sci-fi interface that feels straight out of a thriller film. Space enthusiasts, educators, and developers exploring real-time geospatial visualization will find it both useful and immediately shareable.
